SOP-01: Check why the business is a suitable prospect, which channel produced the lead and who owns the next action.
Ask Sales/BD to distinguish a response, a booked meeting, interest, readiness to sign and a signed contract.
Check that AM has context before the client meeting, rather than receiving the account after closing.
Lead/contact reference; reason for fit; next meeting/action; pre-contract folder.
No clear service need or next owner: return for qualification; do not represent it as a won account.
SOP-02: Open the actual source notes and proposal; a polished deck alone does not demonstrate research.
Check that every claim is labeled as Observed, Interpretation or Recommendation. Inspect source dates and inaccessible-source disclosures.
Compare proposed deliverables to the available assets and capacity. Do not approve a plan that assumes nonexistent footage or capabilities.
Check the three tiers against proposed scope, actual market-range evidence and previous-price records. No invented market rates.
Ensure Sales/BD has studied the problems and solutions rather than simply forwarding skill output.
Dated research/source register; audit; initial strategy; tier scope comparison; pricing evidence.
Unsupported claim: relabel or verify. Missing pricing evidence: do not present an invented price as market-validated.
SOP-03: Read the meeting brief and identify what changed from the initial assumptions.
Look for an explicit client-readiness-to-sign record; interest or a successful meeting is not the same milestone.
If readiness is absent, keep the actual-strategy working group pending. Sales/BD and AM retain the next pre-sales action.
Actual client brief; meeting notes; readiness status/reference; next action.
Client not ready: remain in pre-sales. Do not start actual-strategy development simply because meeting one happened.
SOP-04: Ask AM for a proposal-versus-actual-brief comparison before accepting the actual strategy.
Work with AM, SM and MB to resolve mismatches in objective, channel, audience, resources, measurement and paid-media assumptions.
Check whether changes affect deliverable quantities, production effort, scope or quotation; do not silently add work.
Keep the proposal, actual strategy and agreed quotation distinguishable. The final strategy in the signing pack must reflect the actual brief.
Readiness evidence; comparison/change log; actual strategy; aligned quotation reference.
Readiness not confirmed: stop this preparation step. Conflicting requirements: AM resolves them with client before promising delivery.
SOP-05: Check the printed brief, actual strategy, agreed quotation and contract refer to the same account and scope; all four must be signed.
Confirm the folder was moved, not copied: before PMP Drive / Quotations / [Client]; after PMP Drive / [Client].
Check quotation records are retained and production folders are organized for the correct client/month.
Confirm AM established the client WhatsApp group and the appropriate stakeholders are included.
Signed four-part pack; folder reference; folder structure; kickoff group membership.
Folder moved but signatures/payment missing: do not infer delivery readiness from folder location.
SOP-06: Determine contract category from the agreed scope, not an assumption about the client.
Social-management-only: require the full contract amount before delivery. Other-services-included: require at least half.
Identify the authorized payment verifier with the owner; this manual does not assign that financial authority automatically to MM or AM.
Separate the post-execution 25% media fee from the upfront contract gate and from the media budget.
Signed scope/category; contract amount; received-funds evidence; named verifier/confirmation; later actual-spend record.
Missing verification: hold contracted production. Do not invent balance dates, tax rules or media funding terms.
SOP-07: Check every task has one accountable holder, its actual brief, a usable output definition, priority, deadline, input links and reviewer.
Check upstream dependencies: the next person should not have to infer missing copy, dimensions, footage, terms or client instructions.
Work through AM to maintain one execution view while heads manage their quality work.
Review workload before promising a date; any numeric capacity limit or SLA must be agreed rather than assumed.
Current task sheet; brief; holder; dates; source/output links; dependencies; review route.
Missing inputs: block and assign follow-up. Multiple contributors without one accountable holder: clarify ownership before handoff.
SOP-08: For content, open the same monthly calendar PPTX used by the team; connect comments to the correct task/item.
For Design/Video, inspect the task/reference and actual revision state; do not demand final Drive archival before final client approval.
Make each comment executable: identify the item, problem, expected change and reason. Record the reviewer and owner response.
Do not close a task because the holder says edits are done; verify through the required review decisions.
Task and calendar references; comments; owner execution responses; updated output version.
Conflicting comments: coordinate one resolved direction before asking the holder to execute both. Unresolved comment: task remains open.
SOP-09: Content: confirm Head of Content review first. Design: confirm Head of Design review first.
Video: perform video-quality review yourself as MM and record it; then record the final internal approval as its own decision.
Review the current output against brief, strategy, accuracy, brand requirements, completeness and the comment history.
Do not treat head approval or MM approval as external client approval.
Quality reviewer decision; MM decision; current output reference/version; resolved-comment history.
Quality fails: return to holder with comments. You are unavailable: use only a confirmed delegate; do not invent an override.
SOP-10: Inspect AM’s presentation manifest: every included deliverable must have its required internal reviews.
Check the presented version is identifiable and the client approval refers to that version and included scope.
If the client rejects one item, ensure AM routes that item to the correct holder and coordinates the required re-review and renewed client decision.
After approval, confirm final Design/Video archive links correspond to approved copies. Content’s working calendar exception remains.
Presentation reference/version; task manifest; internal decisions; external client decision; final archive references.
Client approval not evidenced: hold publication. Material changed after approval: prior approval does not automatically cover that change.
SOP-11: Check SM has the approved calendar/presentation and final assets for the correct account and platform.
Review the publishing schedule, live/scheduled references and community exceptions; SM also handles private-label page replies.
Keep paid activation separate from organic publication. Confirm the applicable agreed plan, authorizations and funding with MB.
If someone asks for an urgent unapproved change, route it back through the relevant reviews; urgency is not an approval state.
Approved calendar; final assets; publishing schedule/live links; reply exceptions; paid authorization references where applicable.
Wrong account, asset, version or approval: do not proceed. Incident already live: use the agreed platform/account authority; document and escalate, not an invented blanket delete rule.
SOP-12: Ask SM for performance and listening reports, not only publication counts. Ask MB for paid performance and actual-spend evidence.
Validate source dates, reporting period, metric definitions and missing-data labels before discussing results.
Calculate the post-execution media fee from the agreed actual-expense basis; do not use planned or unused budget as actual spend.
Translate findings into owned actions and a next-cycle recommendation; do not guarantee growth or fabricate baselines.
SM reports; MB spend/performance; source dates; definitions; action owner/next review; actual-expense fee calculation.
Data missing: mark unverified and assign the access/evidence action. Unagreed fee basis: resolve with authorized commercial/financial authority before final billing.
SOP-13: Ask AM for the outsourced crew, guest and PR arrangements, the task brief and expected outputs.
Ask SM where the collected originals, recipient handoff and BTS output are referenced.
Confirm SM can account for issued/returned memory cards and studio tools; a data handoff does not erase equipment accountability.
If hard drives are used, identify the specific drive and named custodian. Do not assume a universal backup policy or SM custody of all drives.
Enforce the documented role rule: Higgsfield account is only for the two video-editor positions.
Shoot brief/arrangements; media transfer/task reference; receiver; BTS reference; card/tool status; drive location/custodian where used.

Missing data, unreadable files or unaccounted equipment: record the issue, involve AM/SM and authorized leadership; do not format, overwrite or claim completion as a workaround. Backup/format controls must be explicitly adopted.

trainingCases: 1 / Prospect and first meeting

Sales finds a business after reviewing its social channels. Sales/BD prepares an audit, initial strategy and three tiers; AM participates. Meeting one reveals that the client has limited footage and a different target audience.
Capture the actual brief and mismatches. Do not treat the initial skill output as the final actual strategy.
2 / Interest is not readiness
The prospect says “this looks promising” but has not confirmed readiness to sign.
Keep actual-strategy development pending. Sales/BD and AM own the pre-sales next action.
3 / Readiness confirmed
Client confirms readiness to sign.
AM compares proposal with actual brief, then develops the actual strategy with SM/MM/MB. Resolve scope/quotation effects before the printed signing pack.
4 / Signing and folder movement
Client signs the printed brief, actual strategy, agreed quotation and contract. The folder is still in Quotations.
Sales or BD moves the SAME folder out to standalone client location; preserve records. AM opens kickoff group. This does not yet prove delivery payment.
5 / Payment check
The illustrative contract includes other services and totals 10,000 units. Only 4,000 has been verified.
Hold contracted delivery. The required minimum is 5,000. If social-only, the minimum would be 10,000. Verify funds through authorized party.
6 / Production assignment
Required upfront funds are verified. AM creates a content task and a reel task. Footage for the reel is missing.
Content may proceed when its inputs are ready; mark the reel blocked on footage and have AM coordinate it. Keep separate accountable holders.
7 / Content review
Writer submits on task sheet and uploads the monthly calendar. HC returns a caption with comments.
Comments remain on the same calendar/item; task stays open. Writer executes comments and records response; HC reviews, then MM approves.
8 / Video review
Editor submits the reel after footage arrives. MM finds a wrong price at a timestamp.
MM records video-quality feedback. Editor corrects and resubmits. MM quality pass and final internal approval are distinct records.
9 / Client presentation
AM gathers finalized work in one PPTX. Client asks for a design change but has not approved it.
Route the affected task back, keep/reopen it, execute comments and repeat relevant reviews. Do not publish the rejected version.
10 / Approval and execution
Client approves the corrected presentation/version.
Archive final approved Design/Video copies. SM receives approved calendar/presentation and assets, schedules/publishes and manages replies.
11 / Learn and fee
SM prepares performance/listening reports. MB’s plan is executed with verified actual expenses of 8,000 units on the agreed basis.
Review evidence and owned next actions. The illustrative 25% post-execution fee is 2,000; unknown taxes/terms are not invented.
practiceScenarios: Prospect liked the deck; actual strategy is requested before readiness is confirmed.
Hold actual-strategy work. Sales/BD and AM confirm readiness to sign after meeting one before AM/SM/MM/MB develop the actual strategy.
Mixed-service contract of 10,000 units is signed; 5,000 is verified. Can delivery start?
Only if the four-part signed pack and authorized verification are complete; the illustrative 50% minimum is met. If social-only, it is not enough.
The folder is standalone on Drive but payment evidence is missing.
Folder movement is a signature milestone, not payment evidence. Contracted delivery remains held.
Writer uploads a calendar and receives comments. Should a new review calendar be created?
Content comments stay on the same calendar PPTX; keep task/item references and owner execution responses traceable.
HD approved a video. Is that the required video-quality gate?
No. User confirmed MM performs video quality; editors report directly to MM. MM quality and final internal decisions must be recorded.
Holder marks edits done while two reviewer comments remain unresolved.
Task stays open. Holder executes all comments and reviewers decide the required approvals; status text alone does not close the loop.
MM approved the assets; the client has not approved AM’s presentation.
Hold publication. AM presents one finalized PPTX and records final external client approval for that version.
SM only reports that posts were published. What is missing from the role review?
Check private-label calendar collection, strategy, performance reports, listening reports, scheduling and page replies as applicable—not publication alone.
Media plan budget was 20,000, but actual agreed-basis expenses after execution are 8,000.
Illustrative fee is 25% × 8,000 = 2,000, subject to agreed expense definition and terms. Planned budget is not actual spend.
MM is unavailable; a holder wants to self-approve to meet a date.
Use only a confirmed authorized backup; otherwise ask owner to assign authority and record the hold. Urgency does not create an override.
An output changes after client approval.
Identify affected scope/version, repeat applicable internal reviews and renewed client decision before releasing changed material.
Public Reel views are very high; can the report state ad spend was confirmed?
No. Public patterns can inform an interpretation, not confirm paid boosting or spend. Record that ad-account evidence is unavailable.
A designer asks to use the company Higgsfield account because a video editor is busy.
Do not grant use. Higgsfield is restricted to VE-01/VE-02; every other member, including MM, is forbidden from using that account. Coordinate the work through an authorized video editor.
Who arranges the outsourced shoot and who collects its data?

AM coordinates outsourced video/photo crew, guests and PR person. SM collects the footage/photos, hands them to assigned editors/designers, captures BTS and takes full accountability for memory cards/studio tools.
A company hard drive has files on it. Can SM be assumed to own its custody and the files be called backed up?
No. Several drives exist, but drive custody and backup rules are not specified. Identify a named custodian, path and actual evidence; do not infer backup or retention status.
A card transfer is unreadable and someone wants to format it.

Record the issue and involve SM/AM/authorized administrator; do not use destructive formatting as a workaround. Adopt explicit transfer/backup/format authority controls; no policy period is invented here.
